reason: B moves through concrete scenes with people and objects in them — a dawn cattle raid, the horses hauled off San Marco, Tyler handling his dagger at Smithfield — and each episode changes the terms rather than restating them, so the reader is pulled forward. A leans on generalized analytic sentences ('a wall turned scattered local power into a target', 'mercy and massacre were both instruments of a political language') and circles the same thesis about institutions and taxable populations repeatedly, especially across the long Baghdad section, where several paragraphs restate that conquerors need living subjects. B's closing scene lands the chapter's argument in action instead of summarizing it a fourth time.
